change: Flat-list canonical DOM validation compares the private reverse-map path indices to the already validated expected path instead of constructing a second identical key string. Forward map lookup, reverse equality, every node/attribute/text/wrapper/placeholder check and mapped-node count remain mandatory. No DOM-validation result cache or skipped subtree was added.

profile.limits: Unminified Chromium whole-fixture sample with nine passing correctness cases, including untimed assertions/recovery. Not an exclusive edit breakdown. Numeric Wasm names are not mapped to Rust source. Production comparisons below do not enable profiling.

tests: 149 renderer tests passed before the runtime change, including six new identical-HTML clone cases (ol, li, h2, strong, p, ul) that require immediate mapping rejection before observer delivery.
All 1844 browser tests and strict source/test TypeScript passed after the change.
Five full DOM/controller/recovery runs in each of Chromium, Firefox and WebKit passed.
Private packed consumers passed in all three engines; base Node, strict TypeScript and Chromium smoke passed against the same installed packages. Shipping artifact trees were verified unchanged.
measurementMethod: Unchanged production installed-package full-editor fixture, old/new/old/new, three cases at each of 10/100/500 items per engine. Reports are relative to the corresponding consumer. All 108 correctness cases passed. Initial baseline may overlap the tail of DOM qualification; second pair followed its confirmed completion. No host-load control or statistical reliability claim.
interpretation: Chromium edit medians decreased in both pairs; Firefox improvement is small. WebKit ranges vary and include a retained 255 ms candidate outlier. Reduced redundant path serialization is established by code, not a general latency guarantee. No prior WebKit fault is resolved by these runs.
